content.text: Generala is a Cameroonian multi-player elimination card game played in tricks with a 54-card deck including two jokers. Players try to shed all cards; in each game the last player with cards is eliminated from the next game of the series.

First English rules were published in August 2011 from a report by Alexey Lobashev, who learned the game from Takam Ludovic Thierry; a corrected version was published in August 2012 after clarifying misunderstood trick and pickup rules. The game is a popular family game in Cameroon.
One 54-card international pack with two jokers.
Deal all cards one by one counterclockwise. Some players may receive one more card than others.

items.text: Series Elimination: Standard multi-player form where loser of each game sits out next game until one champion remains.
Two-Player Loop: With two players, each individual game has a winner and loser; loser deals next game.
